name: Go Stop
description: Go Stop is a Korean flower-card fishing game in which players capture matching month cards, build scoring combinations, and choose whether to stop for payout or go on for higher risk and reward.
deck: Hanafuda/Hwatu 48-card flower deck, often with optional jokers by table rule

overview.description: Go Stop is a Korean flower-card fishing game in which players capture matching month cards, build scoring combinations, and choose whether to stop for payout or go on for higher risk and reward.
overview.deck: Hanafuda/Hwatu 48-card flower deck, often with optional jokers by table rule

history.origins: Go Stop developed in Korea from Japanese flower-card traditions and became the best-known Korean hwatu fishing game.
timeline: Late 19th Century: Hanafuda cards introduced to Korea.
1950s: Plastic Hwatu cards mass-produced, replacing paper ones.
1980s: Go-Stop rules normalized, distinct from Japanese rules (e.g., introduction of 'Jokers' and 'Bomb' rules).
Present: Played universally during Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving) and Lunar New Year.
history.cultural: It is widely played during Korean holidays and social gatherings, often in multi-hand sessions.
history.evolution: Modern Korean tables added local bonuses and optional jokers while preserving month-matching capture play.

setup.players: 2 or 3 active players; larger groups may rotate players between hands.
setup.deck: 48 hwatu cards (12 months x 4 cards), with optional jokers depending on table rules.
setup.dealing: Two-player game: 10 cards each and 8 to table. Three-player game: 7 cards each and 6 to table. Remaining cards form stock.
setup.equipment: Score sheet or chips for multi-hand accounting.

rules.objective: Reach a valid scoring state through captures, then decide to stop for payout or continue by declaring go.
rules.gameplay: On turn, play one hand card to match month cards in the center layout and capture according to matching rules, then reveal the top stock card and resolve captures again. Special capture events and bonus transfers apply when specific board states occur. When your captures reach the minimum score, you may stop to end the hand and collect, or choose go to continue and increase potential payout while risking a loss to an opponent.
keyRules: Cards match by month (flower), not by conventional suit and rank.
Each turn resolves both a hand play and a stock reveal, with captures after each step.
Go-stop choice is only available after reaching the table's minimum scoring threshold.
Exact bonus and penalty multipliers (including jokers and bombs) must be agreed before play.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the 'Godori' (3 Birds) and 'Gwang' cards. They offer the fastest points.
strategy.intermediate: Go/Stop Calculus: If you have 3 points but your opponent is close to a 'Godori', STOP. Don't risk a 'Go' unless your hand is overwhelming.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: If you have a 'Gwang' in hand but there is no match on the table, holding it prevents opponents from getting the 5 Gwang bonus. However, you risk getting stuck with it if the game ends.
tips: Always capture the bonus Jokers immediately if possible.
In 3-player games, don't let the leader 'Go' too many times; sometimes you must win with a small score just to stop them.

variations.name: Matgo (Two-Player)
variations.description: Two-player rules use different deal size and commonly higher stop threshold than three-player play.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Two-player deal and threshold differ; add engine.constants or dealPattern overrides when sourced.

variations.name: No-Joker Table
variations.description: Play with the base 48-card deck and no joker cards or joker-specific bonuses.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No-joker play uses base deck only; no engine overrides required for this variant.

scoring.description: Scores are built from captured card categories and named combinations; payout multipliers increase after each successful go in many tables.
scoring.winCondition: Hand winner is the first player to stop after reaching threshold, or an opponent who overtakes and ends the hand under agreed rules.

synthesis.shortDescription: Korea's national card game using 48 Hwatu (flower) cards, featuring a risk/reward Go-or-Stop mechanic where players decide whether to cash out or risk everything for higher winnings.
